nodes.label: Client-Side-Only Privacy Architecture
nodes.rationale: All PDF processing runs client-side (WASM/JS) so files never leave the device; the analytics ping deliberately excludes file names/contents to preserve this guarantee even in telemetry.

nodes.label: PKC Rebranding of BentoPDF
nodes.rationale: This fork intentionally rebrands BentoPDF to 'PKC PDF Tools' (theme, shared nav/footer, per-tool header), builds in SIMPLE_MODE with a fixed BASE_URL, and strips the Office-conversion/LibreOffice-WASM feature plus non-English locales to fit Cloudflare's 25 MiB per-asset limit, while leaving the underlying PDF engine unchanged from upstream.

nodes.label: Feature Slimming (Office->PDF & Locale Removal)
nodes.rationale: Office->PDF/LibreOffice-WASM and non-English locales were removed specifically to fit Cloudflare Workers' 25 MiB per-asset limit, not for feature-reduction reasons.

nodes.label: Upstream-First Contribution Policy
nodes.rationale: PDF/WASM functionality fixes are steered upstream to BentoPDF so the whole community benefits, since this fork tracks upstream for that work rather than diverging.

nodes.label: PKC-Specific Packaging Contribution Scope
nodes.rationale: Only PKC-specific packaging (branding/theme, top-pill nav, per-tool header/footer injection, privacy analytics, CSP headers, Cloudflare Worker deploy) is accepted as a contribution here, since the repo is scoped as a source mirror for one deployment.

nodes.label: Private Vulnerability Reporting via GitHub Security Advisories
nodes.norm_label: private vulnerability reporting via github security advisories

nodes.label: Default Canonical-to-bentopdf.com SEO Strategy
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted BentoPDF instances default their canonical/hreflang to bentopdf.com so self-hosters don't compete with the official site on brand search and aren't surfaced to strangers via Google; SITE_URL and ROBOTS_NOINDEX give two independent, combinable overrides.

nodes.label: Static Pre-Rendering i18n Architecture
nodes.rationale: Uses build-time static pre-rendering (generate-i18n-pages.mjs writes dist/{lang}/ files) rather than client-side-only i18n switching, specifically to make every locale SEO-crawlable.

nodes.label: AGPL-3.0 Compliance Requirements
nodes.rationale: AGPL-3.0 requires retaining the producer line/copyright and disclosing the full modified source to any users interacting with a network-deployed instance, which is the stated reason a paid commercial license exists for closed-source use.

nodes.label: Liability Disclaimer & $0.00 Cap
nodes.rationale: Liability is capped at $0.00 given the service is free, and provided 'as is' because file corruption/loss during conversion, while unlikely, is possible and users are advised to keep backups.

nodes.label: Client-Side Processing Privacy Principle
nodes.rationale: Core privacy claim: because processing never leaves the browser, the operator is technically incapable of collecting file content, names, or derived metadata — a stronger guarantee than a mere no-logging policy.

nodes.label: Shared PKC pre-paint theme sync
nodes.rationale: Reads the shared 'theme' localStorage key and sets data-theme before paint so the shared top-pill PKC nav (reused across all PKC toolkit sites) renders in the correct theme without a flash, keeping visual consistency across the multi-tool PKC network.

nodes.label: BentoPDF WASM Proxy Cloudflare Worker
nodes.rationale: Proxies WASM library requests through a Cloudflare Worker to bypass CORS restrictions when loading AGPL-licensed components (PyMuPDF, Ghostscript, CoherentPDF) from external CDN sources; enforces origin validation, rate limiting, file-type/size restrictions and caching, and supports self-hosting by letting operators point the proxy at their own WASM origins via secrets.

nodes.label: BentoPDF Dual Licensing Model (AGPL-3.0 + Commercial)
nodes.rationale: BentoPDF is dual-licensed: AGPL-3.0 for open-source projects that publicly share their full source, and a paid Commercial License (lifetime, $79 via Ko-fi) for proprietary/closed-source use. This lets the project stay open-source while monetizing commercial/closed deployments; contributors' code is licensed under these same terms.

nodes.label: COOP/COEP SharedArrayBuffer Requirement
nodes.rationale: Office file conversion needs SharedArrayBuffer, which requires Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin, Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp, and a secure context. localhost is treated as trustworthy by browsers so it works over plain HTTP for local testing, but LAN IPs (e.g. 192.168.x.x) usually are not, so Word/Excel/PowerPoint conversions require HTTPS when the self-hosted deployment is accessed from other devices on the network.

nodes.label: Offline OCR (Air-Gapped)
nodes.rationale: OCR in air-gapped/offline self-hosted environments needs more than the Tesseract worker and traineddata files -- searchable PDF output also needs OCR text-layer fonts served internally via VITE_OCR_FONT_BASE_URL and the bundled ocr-fonts/ directory.

nodes.label: AGPL-3.0 / Commercial Dual Licensing
nodes.rationale: BentoPDF is dual-licensed so open-source/internal users can use it free under AGPL-3.0, while proprietary/closed-source or SaaS users must buy a Commercial License; no license key is used, to reduce operational friction.

nodes.label: AGPL Components Loaded via CDN
nodes.rationale: BentoPDF does not bundle AGPL-licensed processing libraries (PyMuPDF, Ghostscript, CoherentPDF) in source; they load at runtime from pre-configured CDN URLs so BentoPDF's own code stays under its dual-license and compliance boundaries stay clear.

nodes.label: .mjs MIME Type Fix (Apache)
nodes.rationale: Apache's stock mime.types doesn't map .mjs to application/javascript by default, causing the bundled ES-module PDF viewer (Sign PDF, Form Filler) to fail strict MIME checking; fixed by adding AddType application/javascript .mjs.

nodes.label: SharedArrayBuffer Headers (Apache)
nodes.rationale: LibreOffice WASM (Word/ODT/Excel conversion) requires SharedArrayBuffer, which needs COEP/COOP headers plus a secure context; LAN IP HTTP origins don't count as secure even with headers present.

nodes.label: CloudFront Response Headers Policy (COOP/COEP)
nodes.rationale: Without the response headers policy, SharedArrayBuffer is unavailable and LibreOffice WASM conversions hang at ~55%; without correct Content-Encoding on .gz files, WASM compilation fails.

nodes.label: .mjs Content-Type Fix (S3)
nodes.rationale: S3 defaults .mjs to application/octet-stream which browsers refuse to execute as ES modules; the bundled PDF viewer ships .mjs ES modules and needs the content-type explicitly set to application/javascript.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Pages _headers Config
nodes.rationale: COEP/COOP/CORP headers required for SharedArrayBuffer so LibreOffice WASM (Word/ODT/Excel/PowerPoint conversion) can initialize.

nodes.label: Content-Security-Policy (Build-Time Generated)
nodes.rationale: CSP script-src/connect-src/font-src are generated at build time from VITE_* URL vars, including 'unsafe-eval' because LibreOffice WASM compiles dispatch code via new Function(); air-gapped overrides replace rather than append CDN origins.

nodes.label: Full Air-Gapped Docker Workflow
nodes.rationale: WASM URLs are baked in at build time but files are fetched by the user's browser at runtime, so air-gapped networks must pre-download packages and host them on an internal server reachable by the browser.

nodes.label: Self-Hosted Build / Simple Mode
nodes.rationale: Simple Mode is functionally identical to the Commercial build -- every PDF tool works the same -- it only hides marketing chrome (hero, FAQ, testimonials, footer); it is not a feature-reduced 'lite' version.

nodes.label: SharedArrayBuffer Headers (Nginx)
nodes.rationale: nginx add_header in a location block overrides (does not merge with) server-level add_header, so every location block needs its own COEP/COOP headers.

nodes.label: .mjs MIME Fix (Nginx mime.types)
nodes.rationale: nginx parses mime.types line-by-line; a second application/javascript line is silently ignored on some versions, so mjs must be added to the existing js line rather than a new line.

nodes.label: Adjust Colors Tool
nodes.rationale: Like other image-effect tools, adjust-colors rasterizes each page, so output text is not selectable -- a structural tradeoff versus tools like Background Color that edit PDF content directly.

nodes.label: Background Color Tool
nodes.rationale: Works at the PDF structural level (not rasterization), so text remains selectable/searchable -- contrasts with rasterizing tools like Adjust Colors.

nodes.label: Check shared CSS before changing overlay/compare-tool logic
nodes.rationale: Global canvas positioning rules can hide rendered PDF content while leaving highlight layers visible, so shared CSS must be checked before page logic changes to avoid regressions in the compare tool overlay.

nodes.label: Never leave empty catch {} blocks after type-safety hardening
nodes.rationale: Either guard the risky call up front or catch the error into a variable and handle it intentionally with a safe fallback, warning, or typed default, so failures are not silently swallowed.
nodes.norm_label: never leave empty catch {} blocks after type-safety hardening
nodes.community_name: Never leave any in a bug fix when library types can be narrowed

nodes.label: Keep reusable form creator types in src/js/types
nodes.rationale: Logic modules should import shared types rather than owning them, avoiding duplicated or inline type definitions across logic files and tests.
nodes.norm_label: keep reusable form creator types in src/js/types
nodes.community_name: Keep reusable form creator types in src/js/types

nodes.label: Export shared app types from src/js/types/index.ts via @/types alias
nodes.rationale: Do not import shared types from individual type files or relative types/index paths in feature code or tests, to keep a single canonical import path.
nodes.norm_label: export shared app types from src/js/types/index.ts via @/types alias
nodes.community_name: Keep reusable form creator types in src/js/types

nodes.label: Never leave any in a bug fix when library types can be narrowed
nodes.rationale: After a user correction about type safety, capture the lesson immediately: prefer extracting the logic into a typed helper and adding regression tests for the corrected path.
nodes.norm_label: never leave any in a bug fix when library types can be narrowed
nodes.community_name: Never leave any in a bug fix when library types can be narrowed

nodes.label: Normalize pdf.js document-scoped font name prefixes before comparison
nodes.rationale: pdf.js assigns document-scoped font name prefixes (g_d0_, g_d1_, ...) per loaded document; without normalization, comparing font names across documents produces false positive style changes.
nodes.norm_label: normalize pdf.js document-scoped font name prefixes before comparison
nodes.community_name: Normalize pdf.js document-scoped font name prefixes before comparison

nodes.label: LibreOffice PDF conversion depends on explicit import filters
nodes.rationale: Before concluding soffice or LibreOffice WASM cannot convert pdf -> docx/pptx, test the exact filtered path such as --infilter=writer_pdf_import or --infilter=impress_pdf_import and inspect wrapper code for hardcoded capability gates.
nodes.norm_label: libreoffice pdf conversion depends on explicit import filters
nodes.community_name: Check existing API before rebuilding WASM or forking libraries

nodes.label: LibreOfficeKit documentLoadWithOptions() forwards FilterOptions, not FilterName
nodes.rationale: In the current WASM/LOK build, the options string is forwarded as FilterOptions, not media-descriptor FilterName, so passing FilterName=writer_pdf_import from JS does not force PDF to load as Writer or Impress.
nodes.norm_label: libreofficekit documentloadwithoptions() forwards filteroptions, not filtername
nodes.community_name: Check existing API before rebuilding WASM or forking libraries

nodes.label: Never bundle unrelated features into one patch
nodes.rationale: A compile failure in one bundled feature (e.g. abort API + PDF filter fix) breaks the whole build; split by concern, and if already bundled, surgically remove the broken feature rather than layering a second undo patch on top.
nodes.norm_label: never bundle unrelated features into one patch
nodes.community_name: Never bundle unrelated features into one patch

nodes.label: Confirm header declarations are visible at compile time before adding WASM C++ APIs
nodes.rationale: The OperationType enum was declared in lok.hxx but the .cxx failed because of include ordering or missing header propagation, showing new enums/functions need visibility confirmed in all translation units that use them.
nodes.norm_label: confirm header declarations are visible at compile time before adding wasm c++ apis
nodes.community_name: Never bundle unrelated features into one patch

nodes.label: Carefully update unified diff hunks when removing content
nodes.rationale: When removing hunks: update hunk line counts in @@ headers, remove entire file sections if no +/- lines remain, verify old-side line numbers still match the source since removing earlier hunks shifts offsets, and verify '-' lines match the actual source text character-for-character.
nodes.norm_label: carefully update unified diff hunks when removing content
nodes.community_name: Never bundle unrelated features into one patch

nodes.label: Check existing API before rebuilding WASM or forking libraries
nodes.rationale: The matbee libreoffice-converter already had inputFilter support in ConversionOptions, browser.worker.ts, and buildLoadOptions(); the entire WASM rebuild was unnecessary and replacing browser.worker.global.js with a fork build caused a DeploymentException that broke all LibreOffice conversions.
nodes.norm_label: check existing api before rebuilding wasm or forking libraries
nodes.community_name: Check existing API before rebuilding WASM or forking libraries

nodes.label: Never replace compiled vendor assets unless absolutely necessary
nodes.rationale: Assets such as browser.worker.global.js and soffice.wasm.gz are tightly coupled; a mismatched worker JS + WASM binary causes initialization failures.
nodes.norm_label: never replace compiled vendor assets unless absolutely necessary
nodes.community_name: Check existing API before rebuilding WASM or forking libraries
